*I’d hold shipping for one high-priority bug.*

*P1 — Renewal dates clamp against the wrong month* — `src/schedule.js:6–7`

`nextBillingDate` caps the anchor using the *source* month’s length, then constructs a date in the *following* month. This both skips renewals in short months and loses the original anchor when leaving them:

| From | Anchor | Expected | Actual |
|---|---|---|---|
| Jan 31, 2026 | 31 | Feb 28 | Mar 3 |
| Feb 28, 2026 | 31 | Mar 31 | Mar 28 |
| Jan 31, 2028 | 31 | Feb 29 | Mar 2 |
| Mar 31, 2026 | 31 | Apr 30 | May 1 |

The clamp needs to use the *target month’s* length while retaining the supplied anchor. Add regression tests for short-month entry, recovery to the original anchor afterward, and leap February.

*Validation:* All 5 existing tests pass, but a separate calendar check across 2024–2028 found 66 mismatches in 1,860 month/anchor combinations. The existing scheduling tests miss month-length transitions.

Reviewed `billing-anniversary` at `f73b00d` against `main` at `7f89e48`. No files changed.
